problem:
Express the Maclaurin series expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-x),$ given by

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-x)=-x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}-⋯,\,x\in (-1,1]
$$

using sigma notation.
worked_solution:
The first four terms of the series are

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =-x \\ {a}_{2} & =-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2} \\ {a}_{3} & =-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3} \\ {a}_{3} & =-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can express these terms using a common format, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =-\frac{{x}^{1}}{1} \\ {a}_{2} & =-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2} \\ {a}_{3} & =-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3} \\ {a}_{4} & =-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We deduce that the general formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}=-\frac{{x}^{n}}{n}\,.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-x)=-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{n}.
$$
